title: Weddings
tagline: Weddings: the events, congratulations and the future tense.
canDo: You can get through a Pakistani wedding season, in Urdu

grammar.title: Future tense
grammar.body: Verb stem + ending + ga/gi/ge. main jaunga (I'll go, man), main jaungi (woman), tum jaoge, woh jayega/jayegi, hum/aap jayenge. The ga/gi/ge matches the speaker's gender and number, and in Urdu script it's written as a separate word: جاؤں گا.

phrases.en: the reception, hosted by the groom's family
drum night: singing, clapping, aunties' songs
Happy wedding! (to the couple or family)
When will the food be served?
phrases.note: Asked at every wedding at 11pm. Food is served at 1am.
Said by every aunty to every single person at every wedding.

lessons.title: Shaadi vocab
lessons.blurb: Mehndi, baraat, walima: a wedding is three to five events. Minimum.
lessons.canDo: You can name the events and people of a Pakistani wedding

teach.title: A wedding is a season
teach.info: Dholki nights (weeks before), mehndi, baraat (the wedding day), walima (reception). Each is a separate outfit. Each is late. Each has biryani.

teach.tip: Cash in an envelope. The amount will be discussed by aunties for years.

exercises.prompt: Type: “bride”
Which event is hosted by the groom's family, after the wedding?
The henna night is called…

lessons.title: Mubarak ho!
lessons.blurb: Congratulate everyone. Then congratulate them again.
lessons.canDo: You can congratulate the family and reply to congratulations

teach.tip: Works for weddings, babies, exam results, new cars.
If someone says mubarak to you, this is the reply.
Say this. Mean it. It is always true at a wedding.

exercises.prompt: You walk into the mehndi and see the bride's mother.
Someone says “Mubarak ho!” to you (your cousin is the bride).
Type: “Congratulations!”
Reply to a congratulations

lessons.title: Main naachunga
lessons.blurb: The future tense, featuring the dance-floor ultimatum.
lessons.canDo: You can say what you will and won't do

teach.title: Future: -unga, -ungi, -enge
teach.info: Stem + unga (I, man) / ungi (I, woman) / enge (we, aap). Naach (dance): main naachunga, main naachungi, hum naachenge. Ga/gi/ge is written as a separate little word in Urdu script.

teach.tip: Nahin goes right before the verb.

exercises.prompt: You're a woman and Khala insists. Agree to dance.
You're a man and you will NOT be dancing.
You're a guy. Type: “I'll dance”
Type: “We'll go tomorrow”

lessons.title: Agla number tumhara!
lessons.blurb: Every wedding conversation with an aunty, and how to escape it.
lessons.canDo: You can survive 'you're next!' and 'when are you getting married?'

teach.tip: Future tense again: karoge = will you do.
The question everyone is secretly asking.

boss.title: The Mehndi
boss.blurb: Your cousin's mehndi. Khala wants you on the dance floor. Mrs. Butt wants you on her list.
boss.scene: Yellow and orange everywhere, a dhol thumping, three hundred guests. You've barely stepped in when Shabnam Khala spots you from across the lawn and starts marching over.
boss.canDo: You can get through a wedding event: congratulate, dance (or refuse), and deflect the rishta questions

b.prompt: Greet her. (Her daughter is the bride.)

options.reaction: An excuse before a congratulations. Bold sequencing.

d.prompt: She's pulling you to the dance floor.

options.reaction: The dhol player nods at you. You are now a dancer.

g.prompt: Mrs. Butt has entered the chat.

options.reaction: Flawless deflection. Nobody can resist talking about the bride.

end.title: Mehndi survived
end.text: You congratulated, (maybe) danced, and deflected two rishta attacks. Food arrived at 1:14am. You were there for it.
